title: Method for culture and maintenance of long term primary human fungiform taste cells
protocol: Collect fungiform papillae from the dorsal surface of the tongue using curved spring microscissors and place them immediately into an isolation solution.
Dissolve one package of MCDB 153 (17.6 grams) in one liter of tissue culture grade water completely.
Supplement dissolved MCDB 153 with 1.18 g/L sodium bicarbonate according to manufacturer instructions.
Check the pH, which should be between 7.0 and 7.1.
Store the prepared medium at 4°C and protect from light.
Cover the bottle containing the medium with aluminum foil.

Mix Iscove's Modified Dulbecco’s medium (Gibco BRL), 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS, BTI), a 1:5 ratio of MCDB 153 (Sigma), and a triple cocktail of antibiotics (100U/ml / 100μg/ml Penicillin/Streptomycin, 2.5μg/ml Gentamycin, and 0.5μg/ml Fungizone) to prepare taste cell culture medium.
Cover the bottle containing the taste cell culture medium with aluminum foil.
Use the prepared taste cell culture medium within three months or less.
Dissolve 2.1 g NaHCO3, 0.3 g NaH2PO4, 3.6 g glucose, 3.77 g NaCl, 1.48 g KCl, and 0.372 g EDTA in nuclease-free water.
Filter sterilize the solution.
Treat coverslips with 2M NaOH for 1 hour.
Leave treated coverslips overnight in 70% nitric acid (HNO3).
Wash coverslips with 9M HCl for 1 hour.
Autoclave coverslips in water and rinse with 70% ethanol and 100% ethanol.
Air dry the coverslips.
Dilute rat tail collagen type-1 (3.96 mg/ml) with sterile nuclease-free water at a 1:4 ratio.
Add 0.5 - 1 ml of diluted rat tail collagen type-1 onto coverslips in a 12-well tissue culture plate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the collagen solution and let coverslips air dry for 10-20 minutes.
Mix collagenase (550 U/ml), elastase (10 U/ml), and trypsin inhibitor (0.9 mg/ml) in calcium-free Ringer's solution just before use.
Dissolve 145 g NaCl, 0.373 g KCl, 0.203 g MgCl2, 0.147 g CaCl2, and 0.110 g sodium pyruvate in 1 liter of water.
Add 4.76 g Hepes-Na to the solution.
Adjust pH to 7.1 - 7.2.
Adjust osmolarity to 300-310 mOsmol.
Dissolve 145 g NaCl, 0.373 g KCl, 0.203 g MgCl₂, 0.110 g Na-pyruvate, and 4.76 g Hepes-Na in 1 liter water.
Adjust pH to 7.1 to 7.2 for the calcium-free Ringer solution.
Adjust osmolarity to 300-310 mOsmol for the calcium-free Ringer solution.
Dissolve 4.67 g NaCl, 0.373 g KCl, 0.203 g MgCl₂, 0.147 g CaCl₂, 0.110 g Na-pyruvate, and 4.76 g Hepes-Na in 1 liter water.
Adjust pH to 7.1 to 7.2 for the modified Ringer solution.
Adjust osmolarity to 300-310 mOsmol using 5M NaCl for the modified Ringer solution.
Filter sterilize the modified Ringer solution.
Add DMSO into Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS) to make a final volume of 5%.
Keep DMSO tightly closed and replace frequently due to its physiologic properties when oxidized.
Remove four to eight human fungiform taste papillae from the dorsal surface of the anterior portion of the tongue using sterile curved spring microscissors and sterile glassware and tubing.
Place the removed taste papillae immediately into an isolation solution.
Digest human fungiform taste cell papillae using enzymatic digestion protocol for 30-45 minutes.
Incubate fungiform papillae with collagenase, elastase and soybean trypsin inhibitor in a 35°C water bath with circulation for 30 minutes and gentle oxygenation with 95% O2/5% CO2.
Wash papillae with Ringer's solution.
Triturate the papillae 10 times with a fire-polished glass Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge the mixture for 3 minutes at 2500 rpm at room temperature.
Remove the isolation solution and add 1 ml of taste cell culture medium.
Transfer digested fungiform papillae into a glass dish.
Finely mince the fungiform papillae gently with a surgical razor.
Add 150-250 μl of minced papillae into a cloning cylinder onto a rat tail collagen type-1 coated coverslip.
Add 1 ml of taste cell culture medium to each well.
Incubate plate at 36°C in a humidified incubator containing 5% CO₂.
Place plate undisturbed in the incubator for 2-3 days prior to the first change of complete medium.
Remove cloning cylinder from the plate and medium completely.
Add 1 ml of taste cell medium into each well.
Check cell growth under the microscope every other day.
Replace 1/3 of the medium every 6-7 days.
Once 80-100% of the cloning cylinder is covered with cells, trypsinize cells using 0.25% w/v trypsin/EDTA for 2-3 minutes at 36°C.
Transfer cells from wells into 15 ml tubes.
Add 3 volumes of taste cell culture medium followed by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells with 1 ml of taste cell medium.
Transfer cells into the T25 plate.
Add 4 ml of taste cell medium.
Maintain cells at 36°C in a humidified incubator containing 5% CO₂.
Replace 1/3 of the medium every 6-7 days until cultured taste cells have reached 100% confluence.
Wash cells once with sterile PBS when they reach close to 100% confluence.
Trypsinize cells using 0.25% w/v trypsin/EDTA for 2-3 minutes at 36°C.
Centrifuge the cells as described above.
Resuspend in complete taste cell medium.
Transfer cells to fresh T-75 flasks (passage 1).
Replace 1/3 of the medium every 6-7 days after transferring to T-75 flasks.
Split cells to no more than a 1:4 dilution in a T75 flask when they reach close to 100% confluence.
After trypsinization, add complete taste cell medium and transfer cells to sterile 15 ml conical centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 2500 rpm for 5 min at room temperature.
Carefully discard the supernatant and gently resuspend cells with appropriate 1 ml of freezing medium.
Transfer cells to labeled, sterile cryovials, cap tightly, and place in a freezing container containing isopropanol.
Place into a -80°C freezer for at least one day prior to transferring indefinitely to liquid nitrogen.
To thaw a vial of frozen primary human fungiform taste cells, place at 37°C water bath until just thawed (approximately 1 minute) while working in a laminar-flow cell culture hood.
Transfer cells and freezing medium to a sterile 15 ml conical centrifuge tube and add 5 ml of taste cell culture medium.
Centrifuge cells at 2500 rpm for 5 min at room temperature.
Carefully discard supernatant, gently resuspend cells with complete taste cell culture medium, and transfer to a sterile T-25 tissue culture flask.
Continue to culture cells according to Step 16 to 25 until cells show evidence of senescence.
Base evidence of senescence on viability, proliferation rate, and functional properties.
Typically perform experiments using cells at passage-2 through -7.
Cells may be used beyond passage number 7 if appropriate.
